Subject: HIPAA scope & hosting clarification — security intake and next steps

Hi Tom / Emily —

Thanks again for taking the demo and the deep dive today. Quick recap and proposed intake plan so we can line up procurement and engineering: 

Call recap (high level)
- You are evaluating Redwood to provide AI-assisted triage and patient summary generation for a subset of outpatient lab results and structured clinical notes.
- PHI types you flagged as in-scope: patient identifiers (MRN, name/dob), lab results (numeric and coded), and clinician free-text notes. You confirmed medical imaging (DICOM files) are out of scope for the initial phase.
- Procurement target: decision by end of October; pilot expected in November if security sign-off occurs.

Security and hosting options (short)
- Hosted API (Redwood-managed keys): NOT recommended for PHI unless customer obtains a dedicated, isolated instance plus BAA. By default, public hosted endpoints are not approved for PHI.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, isolated tenancy): BAA-compatible; supports stricter network isolation, optional BYOK for encryption-at-rest.
- Private (VPC / customer-controlled network) or on-prem: preferred for full PHI handling and customer-managed keys.

Controls and status
- SOC 2: Redwood currently has SOC 2 Type I (controls design) and is in process for Type II; anticipated Type II completion Q1 2027.
- Data protection: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. Audit logging with token-level traces available for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Key management: Customer-managed keys (BYOK) available for Private deployments and selectable for Dedicated (depends on contract). Hosted-managed keys remain Redwood-owned.

Next steps / mutual action plan
1) I will send our Security Questionnaire (attached) and a draft BAA for your legal team to review — action: Marissa — due: 2026-09-15 EOD.
2) You to confirm final in-scope PHI types + technical admin contact for IT/procurement (name, email, phone) — action: Tom — due: 2026-09-17.
3) Security to review questionnaire and flag any product gaps; Engineering to assess Private deployment POC effort if needed — action: Redwood (security + eng) — due: 2026-09-23.
4) If BAA terms are acceptable, legal will route an execution path (DocuSign or contract amendment) to meet your procurement timeline — action: mutual — target: end of Oct.

Attachments included: Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx, draft BAA (BAA_Template_Draft_MedSys.pdf). Also sharing call recording: https://drive.google.com/recording/medsys-20260914

Please let me know any immediate clarifications. If you prefer, we can carve a short technical sync next week (30 minutes) to walk engineers through network diagrams and key management options.

Best,
Marissa

Tom — appreciate the detail. Answers inline below and next actions.

> For Dedicated deployments, do you support customer-controlled key rotation (BYOK) with HSM-backed keys? Who would be the key escrow holder during emergency access?
- Yes, Dedicated supports BYOK with HSM-backed keys (we integrate with major cloud KMS providers for CMKs). For Private/on-prem, the customer is the key owner and controls rotation. For Dedicated BYOK, we can document emergency access procedures: Redwood does not hold customer keys; emergency access (for platform operations) requires a documented escalation and is auditable — key escrow is customer-controlled or via a mutually agreed legal process. We can include specific escrow language in the BAA if needed.

> For audit logs: can you provide exportable, customer-filterable logs (S3-compatible export) with 90-day retention by default and longer retention options?
- Yes. Dedicated and Private deployments provide exportable audit logs; default retention for hosted logs is 90 days, with configurable longer retention for Dedicated/Private. Logs are exportable to S3-compatible endpoints; we will capture token-level request/response metadata (not full PHI payloads unless configured for your POC).

> Does the draft BAA include breach notification SLAs (24-hour notification window)?
- Our standard BAA template includes 48-hour notification by default; we can discuss 24-hour escalation clauses with Legal. I'll flag this with our GC team.

Next actions (updated)
- I attached the Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx (filled partially with our controls). Please complete the customer columns where you can; we'll mark product-level controls on our side.
- Legal: I attached a draft BAA (BAA_Template_Draft_MedSys.pdf). Please share any redlines once your procurement/legal review it.
- Can you provide the technical admin contact and an IP range (if you want IP allowlisting) by 2026-09-17?

If it helps, Karthik (cc'd) can do a 30-minute technical call next Tue (09/21) to walk through network diagrams, VPC peering options, and the key management flow.

I'll start an internal intake to scope a Private deployment POC and will loop Rishi for compliance gap review.

Regards,
Marissa
